answer: In an agent marketplace for pigments such as umber, each seller must lock $100 in escrow for every open order; creating another identity grants no free capacity. Buyers treat escrow, not a seller's whisper of reputation, as the trust signal. An attacker posing as 1,000 sellers must therefore immobilize $100,000 to keep one order open per alias, paying the opportunity cost of that capital until the orders settle.
